The exported components are not in our source tree. Also Play Console warned about a new READ_PHONE_STATE permission. We upgraded an analytics SDK from 4.1 to 4.2 in this release. The debug manifest in CI looked fine; the release build uses a different flavor dependency (releaseImplementation).
questions.promptHtml: Run the post-incident review: how did it happen, how do you contain it, and how do you prevent it?

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Remove it from the manifest and ship." They don't identify where it came from, whether the removal breaks the SDK, whether other apps already read data, and don't add any process.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Which exact merged entries are new vs previous release? Is the data actually exposed (do the components act on extras)? Did anyone exploit it (any telemetry)? Is READ_PHONE_STATE needed by SDK 4.2 features we use? Which build variant did the pentest use?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Diff merged manifests of 11.x vs 12.0 release (apkanalyzer manifest print, or the merger report). Add tools:node="remove" for the debug activity and, if the receiver is unneeded, for it; or set android:exported="false" with tools:replace="android:exported". Hotfix with staged rollout; consider halting rollout in the meantime.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) SDK 4.2's release variant manifest ships an exported debug component; (b) a different artifact in releaseImplementation brings it; (c) our own manifest regression (red herring: the pentest report named an app package prefix, but it's the SDK's); (d) permission came from a transitive dependency.
  4. How I'd verify each: manifest-merger-release-report.txt (it names the source library for each line); Android Studio Merged Manifest view for the release variant; ./gradlew :app:dependencies --configuration releaseRuntimeClasspath; adb shell dumpsys package com.app shows exported components; Compare with SDK release notes.
  5. Root cause: Manifest merging adds library components with whatever exported the library declares; our process only reviewed source and the debug merged manifest, so the SDK's release-only content was never seen.
  6. Fix: Short-term: removal markers.
<activity android:name="com.app.sdk.DebugOverlayActivity" tools:node="remove" />
<receiver android:name="com.app.sdk.PushReceiver"
    android:exported="false" tools:replace="android:exported" />
<uses-permission android:name="android.permission.READ_PHONE_STATE" tools:node="remove" />

Then confirm the SDK still works (smoke tests); ask the vendor for a fix. Long-term: pin SDK versions, evaluate vendor. 7. Prevention: CI step that exports the merged manifest of every variant and fails on any diff in exported=true components, permissions or <queries> unless a reviewer updates a golden file; SDK upgrade checklist; security review of dependency manifests; Play pre-launch report. 8. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: Not blanket removeAll on components (breaks needed SDK pieces); not ignoring the permission warning (Play data safety form must match). Removing a permission an SDK feature depends on yields a runtime SecurityException; test that path.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Vendor refuses to fix? → Replace the SDK or wrap with permission guards; document the risk.
  • Is exported=false enough? → For the component yes; the data leak in logs is a separate bug to fix (no sensitive data in logs).
  • How do you detect this at dependency-bump time? → Renovate/Dependabot PR job producing a manifest diff comment.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A debug-only deep link host shipped in a vendor AAR for two quarters; discovered only when a security researcher opened it from adb.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: edits the manifest without finding the source, no process change.
  • Hire: merger report, tools markers, release-variant check.
  • Strong hire: CI manifest golden-file diff, Play data-safety alignment, and risk of breaking SDK behavior.

questions.contextHtml:
A matrimony app (1.2M DAU, 60% Hindi/regional) shipped an in-app language picker. Support tickets: "I chose Hindi but notifications and the home-screen widget are English", and "after rotation, dialogs flip to English on Android 12". Code:

class BaseActivity : AppCompatActivity() {
    override fun attachBaseContext(newBase: Context) {
        val cfg = Configuration(newBase.resources.configuration)
        cfg.setLocale(Locale.forLanguageTag(Prefs.lang))   // Prefs uses a lateinit Application
        super.attachBaseContext(newBase.createConfigurationContext(cfg))
    }
}
class NotifBuilder(private val app: Application) {
    fun title() = app.getString(R.string.match_title)
}

Crashlytics also shows a rare UninitializedPropertyAccessException: lateinit property app has not been initialized from Prefs, mostly from BaseActivity.attachBaseContext on Android 7-8 during process restore.
questions.promptHtml: What are the bugs and what is the right design?

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Call recreate() after changing language." This doesn't address Services/notifications, the lateinit crash, or AppCompat's own configuration handling.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Minimum OS (affects per-app language availability)? Does the app use AppCompat night mode too? Where is Prefs.lang initialized and when? Which components render localized text outside Activities (notifications, widgets, WorkManager)?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Fix the crash first: read prefs from newBase, not an Application-held field that may not exist yet (attachBaseContext runs before Application.onCreate only for the Application's own call chain, but a restored Activity can execute while a static is uninitialized after provider/reflection ordering). Ship a hotfix.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) override only wraps Activities; Application context/Services stay in system locale; (b) setLocale on a copy without setLocales loses the fallback list; (c) AppCompat 1.2+ re-applies its own configuration, clobbering the wrapper on night-mode changes (the rotation/dialog flip on Android 12); (d) lateinit timing.
  4. How I'd verify each: Set system language to English, in-app Hindi, trigger a notification and a rotation; log resources.configuration.locales for Activity, applicationContext, Service; adb shell dumpsys activity for configuration; test with Don't-keep-activities.
  5. Root cause: Configuration overrides are per-context. Only the Activity base is wrapped; the notification builder uses the Application's untouched Resources. The lateinit read depends on startup order, and AppCompat's applyOverrideConfiguration can replace the hand-built configuration.
  6. Fix: Use the platform: AppCompatDelegate.setApplicationLocales(...) (AppCompat 1.6+; delegates to LocaleManager on API 33+, persists with AppLocalesMetadataHolderService autoStoreLocales on older) and add locales_config. For non-Activity text, build strings with a localized context:
fun Context.localized(tag: String): Context {
    val c = Configuration(resources.configuration)
    c.setLocales(LocaleList.forLanguageTags(tag))
    return createConfigurationContext(c)
}
NotificationCompat.Builder(ctx.localized(tag), CH)
    .setContentTitle(ctx.localized(tag).getString(R.string.match_title))
  1. Prevention: Instrumented test per entry point (Activity, Service, notification, widget) with a non-system locale; string wrappers (UiText) resolved at the edge; lint for updateConfiguration.
  2. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: Not resources.updateConfiguration (deprecated, global mutation). Not Locale.setDefault alone (JVM global, doesn't change Resources). Platform API changes also affect Settings integration, which is a benefit.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Widgets (RemoteViews)? → Inflated by the launcher with its own context; set text strings at update time from your localized context.
  • RTL? → Locale change also flips layout direction; use start/end, test Urdu/Arabic.
  • Server-side push text? → Send localized payloads or locale keys; client rendering needs the same override.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A "language switch" feature passed QA on Activities but a push campaign shipped English titles to a Tamil-heavy cohort for a week.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: recreate() only.
  • Hire: identifies per-context scope and prefers AppCompat/LocaleManager.
  • Strong hire: handles non-Activity surfaces, the init-order crash, AppCompat override interaction, and testing matrix.

questions.contextHtml:
After adding an in-app Light/Dark/System toggle (AppCompatDelegate.setDefaultNightMode), support receives screenshots: users who set app = Dark while system = Light see a dark screen with unreadable dark-grey text in the "Payment methods" bottom sheet and the toast-like snackbar helper. 9% of sessions use that sheet. System=Dark + app=Light shows the opposite. Helper code:

class SheetHelper(private val context: Context) { // constructed with applicationContext
    fun inflate(): View =
        LayoutInflater.from(context).inflate(R.layout.sheet_payment, null)
    fun textColor() = context.getColor(R.color.text_primary)
}

R.color.text_primary has a values-night variant. QA tested only with matching system and app settings.
questions.promptHtml: Diagnose it, fix it, and explain why QA missed it.

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Add -night resources" (already there) or "force dark theme". Misses that the contexts disagree about night.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Does it happen only when app and system disagree? Is the sheet inflated via the Activity or a helper? Is configChanges="uiMode" set? Compose or Views? Which AppCompat version?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Constrain the toggle's blast radius if needed (feature flag to hide it), or hotfix the helper to take the Activity context.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) helper holds the Application context, which sees the system uiMode; (b) cached colors/drawables across toggles; (c) configChanges swallowing recreation; (d) theme missing DayNight parent (red herring: other screens are right, so the theme is fine).
  4. How I'd verify each: Log context.resources.configuration.uiMode for activity vs application when app=Dark/system=Light; layout inspector theme attrs; reproduce with adb shell cmd uimode night yes while the app is forced to light.
  5. Root cause: AppCompatDelegate applies its night override as an override configuration on the Activity's base context only. The Application context keeps the system uiMode, so inflating or reading colors through it resolves values-night according to the system, not the in-app choice. It also lacks the Activity theme.
  6. Fix: Pass the Activity (or ContextThemeWrapper) at call time, or resolve with theme attributes (MaterialColors.getColor(view, R.attr.colorOnSurface)), and avoid storing contexts:
fun inflate(activity: Activity): View =
    LayoutInflater.from(activity).inflate(R.layout.sheet_payment, null)

Long-term: stop referencing raw color resources in views; use ?attr/ theme attributes. 7. Prevention: Screenshot tests (Paparazzi/Roborazzi) in 2x2 matrix {system light/dark} x {app light/dark}; lint/detekt rule against storing applicationContext in UI helpers; QA matrix updated. 8. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: Not duplicating dark colors per screen; not configChanges="uiMode" to avoid recreation (stale UI risk), though it can be right for media apps; not forceDarkAllowed, which masks real defects.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Compose? → Pass through MaterialTheme; isSystemInDarkTheme() is system-based, so honor the app setting in your own AppTheme(darkTheme = ...).
  • Notifications? → They're rendered by SystemUI in the system theme; don't expect the app toggle to apply.
  • Does Android 13's per-app theme change this? → API 31+ UiModeManager.setApplicationNightMode makes the platform own the override, reducing the mismatch.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A design-system PR replaced theme attributes with hard-coded color resources "for performance", and the inconsistent night behavior only appeared in the 4% who overrode system mode.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
• No hire: adds more resource variants.
  • Hire: Application vs Activity configuration explanation, passes Activity context.
  • Strong hire: theme attributes, 2x2 test matrix, screenshot tests, and caveats about system-rendered surfaces.

questions.contextHtml: App on Play as an AAB, 4M MAU, with an in-app language picker (en, hi, ta, te, bn, mr). After release 9.4 (built with AGP 8.x, nothing in the bundle config changed), Crashlytics shows Resources$NotFoundException rate 0.3% and a flood of support tickets: "app is in English after I chose Tamil", concentrated on users whose system language is English (91% of reports). Fresh installs on internal test tracks look fine; the QA team always installs with a Tamil system language. The universal APK built by CI works for everyone. A new config.ta.apk split appears for only some users in Play Console device catalog.
questions.promptHtml: What is happening and what is the durable fix?

sections.label: What a weak answer looks like
sections.html: "Add Tamil strings again", "Clear data". This ignores the delivery layer and that the same code works in a universal APK.

sections.label: Strong answer
sections.html:
1. Clarifying questions I'd ask: Does the problem occur only for installs from Play (not sideload of universal APK)? Is it only for languages different from the system's? Does it fix itself after Play updates? Android versions of affected devices (Play delivers language splits per system locales)?
  2. Immediate mitigation: Disable language splitting in the bundle config and publish a hotfix so all languages are in the base/config for everyone; in parallel inform support to tell users to re-select the language after the update.
  3. Hypotheses, ranked: (a) Play installs only the language config splits matching the device's system locales at install time, so Tamil strings are absent for English-system users; (b) a ProGuard/shrinker change removed resources (red herring: universal APK would break too); (c) per-app locale persisted but resource lookup fell back to default; (d) a stale split cache.
  4. How I'd verify each: bundletool build-apks --connected-device --device-spec with an English-locale device spec and inspect installed splits (adb shell pm path <pkg> shows which split_config.*.apk exist); compare Tamil spec; Internal App Sharing install on a device with English system; aapt2 dump resources.
  5. Root cause: Bundles split resources by language into config APKs. By default Play delivers only the languages in the user's system language list. An in-app locale not in that list has no installed strings, so lookups fall back to default values/ (English) or throw NotFoundException for locale-only resources. The universal APK has everything, so CI looked fine. Note: newer Play versions can fetch additional languages on demand when the user changes the system/per-app language through the platform APIs, but custom in-app pickers bypass that.
  6. Fix: Short-term, disable language splits:
// app/build.gradle.kts
android {
    bundle {
        language { enableSplit = false }
    }
}

Cost: larger download (strings for all languages, usually small, a few hundred KB to low MB). Long-term: use the per-app language APIs (AppCompatDelegate.setApplicationLocales / LocaleManager) so the Play side can install the language split on demand, and/or use Play Feature Delivery's SplitInstallRequest.addLanguage(Locale) to request a language before switching, with a fallback UI.

val req = SplitInstallRequest.newBuilder()
    .addLanguage(Locale.forLanguageTag("ta")).build()
manager.startInstall(req)
  1. Prevention: Test with bundletool --connected-device on devices with a mismatched system language, run an install-from-Internal-App-Sharing check per release, keep the QA matrix on {system locale} x {in-app locale}, and add a startup log of installed splits to telemetry.
  2. Trade-offs & what I'd NOT do: Not shipping only the universal APK outside Play to hide it (loses Play benefits). Not removing all splits (ABI/density splits give the real savings); disabling only language splits keeps most size gains.

sections.label: Curveball follow-ups
sections.html:
• Size impact too high? → Measure it: for an app with 6 languages the language split is typically small; if not, request languages on demand.
  • Does this affect dynamic feature modules? → Yes, each feature has its own config splits, so languages must be requested for them too.
  • Device uses sideloaded APKs? → Not affected, since APK sets installed via bundletool --connected-device get device-specific splits, but a universal APK doesn't.

sections.label: Senior war story
sections.html: A localization launch for a new market looked perfect on QA phones set to that language; the first-week retention dip in the market came from users whose phones were set to English.

sections.label: Scoring rubric
sections.html:
